newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila senator denies links to alleged drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Manila senator denies links to alleged drug lord.

text.p: A popular Philippine senator, who has announced plans to run for vice president in next year's presidential elections, on Tuesday denied involvement in the illegal drugs trade.
Vicente Sotto, in a speech to the Senate, also disowned any links with policemen alleged to be protecting a suspected Filipino-Chinese drug lord.
"I was not, am not and never will be associated with any aspect of the manufacture, distribution and sale of illegal drugs and substances," he said.

Newspapers, quoting police, said two policemen assigned as security aides to Sotto also worked for a Filipino-Chinese businessman suspected of running a drug syndicate. The businessman is reported to have recently fled to Hong Kong.
Sotto, head of the Senate committee on illegal drugs, denied the two policemen were part of his staff and that the reports were politically motivated to smear his reputation.
He said he met the businessman casually last year, had only superficial dealings with him and did not know the businessman was being linked to drug trafficking.
Sotto, a member of a TV comedy team before entering politics, topped the 1992 senatorial elections and is rated in opinion polls as a strong vice presidential contender in next year's elections.
